summary: Outpost Cadet is an interactive Flutter game that lets kids ages 7–12 run a Moon or Mars outpost and learn deep-space survival through play, not quizzes. Players build a small base under mass and power budgets, balance life support, radiation shielding, power, and food, then walk a top-down outpost and face events like dust storms, lunar dust, and solar flares. Every decision has a real cost, mirroring how NASA mission planners trade limited resources. Space-weather risk can come from NASA’s DONKI solar-flare data (live or a clearly labeled cached snapshot), and Mars missions teach communication delay so players decide before Earth advice arrives. Debrief screens unlock NASA- and CSA-cited fact cards so learning sticks. The project matters because Artemis and Mars exploration are no longer hypothetical: the next generation needs to feel the same trade-offs that keep crews alive beyond Earth—fun enough to finish, accurate enough to teach.
details:
What it does / how it works
Outpost Cadet is a junior astronaut mission trainer for ages 7–12. Players pick a Moon or Mars mission, see a NASA DONKI–based space-weather briefing (live flares when online, or a clearly labeled cached snapshot offline), then build a 3×3 outpost under mass and power budgets. They walk a top-down base, inspect modules, advance sols/days, and face events—dust storms, lunar dust, solar flares, equipment glitches, and delayed Earth advice. Four meters stay in view: LIFE, SHIELD, POWER, and FOOD. Every choice costs something. After the mission, a debrief scores the run and unlocks NASA- and CSA-cited fact cards.

Benefits
It turns abstract “space survival” into a playable system: kids feel trade-offs (power vs food, shelter vs science, act now vs wait for Earth) instead of memorizing facts. Replayability comes from mission variety, weather tiers, and different strategies. Parents and educators get a clear learning loop with traceable sources.

Intended impact
As Artemis and Mars exploration move from fiction to planning, the next generation should understand why every watt, liter, and kilogram matters. Outpost Cadet aims to put kids in the commander’s seat so they leave knowing real constraints of living beyond Earth—not just that space is “cool.”

Tools / languages / hardware / software

  • Languages & frameworks: Dart, Flutter
  • Game/UI: Flame (2D walkable world), Riverpod, go_router, Material UI
  • Data & storage: JSON content packs, http for DONKI, shared_preferences
  • NASA / partner data: DONKI (live + cache), curated RadLab/OSDR/Mars Trek/CSA food facts
  • Platforms: Android (release APK primary); web demo supported
  • Dev tools: Flutter SDK, Android SDK/Gradle, git

Creativity
The bridge is play + truth: a walkable outpost with cinematic events, Mix Path roads, and inspect speech—not a quiz—while mechanics mirror real mission math. Live space weather can change how risky flares feel; Mars radio delay (~20 min) vs near-instant lunar contact teaches autonomy. Moon and Mars tracks share one engine with different physics of dust and delay.

Factors the team considered
Audience (plain language, ages 7–12); no “free” safe choices; keep four clear meters without overwhelming systems; honesty about live vs cached NASA data; Moon and Mars both allowed by the challenge; Android/web reach for judging; educational payoff via cited debriefs; solo scope focused on a working prototype that proves the trade-off mechanic clearly.
